analysis.title: "Somebody Wants Out!": McElligott Warns If Stocks Can't Rally With Every Machine Primed To Buy, It's Not A Positioning Problem
key_insights: Nomura's McElligott argues a mechanical, vol-reset-driven relief rally is possible after this week's four risk events (NVDA earnings, VIX expiry, Anthropic IPO, Friday OpEx). He says the view's wide acceptance is its largest headwind and raises 'Sellers are LOWER' risk if spot keeps breaking.

Three of the four events have cleared. NVDA was 'extremely strong and raising guide', the Anthropic IPO had 'impossibly low allocations', and VIX expiry had 'no VIX Gamma to squeeze'. Nasdaq futures' early 2% gain faded and the S&P slid back below its 200-day moving average by mid-morning Thursday.

Much of the gamma rolling off at Friday's expiry is dealer long gamma, so the market loses some stabilizing flow. McElligott still sees a 'significant Short Gamma' market into next week, which can feed 'large TWO-WAY moves' in the direction the market is already heading.

Rally fuel sits in vanna. If high implied vol, stressed vol-of-vol and steep skew reset lower, dealers' short puts lose delta and dealers must buy back short futures hedges, which generates mechanical futures buying.

Nomura's CTA model shows clustered buy triggers as short-term trend windows flip. About $7.9B of global equity futures buying triggers on a 2% rally and $21.1B on a 4% rally, including $9.3B in the S&P alone. Trend signals for the S&P, Russell, Nasdaq, Nikkei, TOPIX and FTSE sit at -8 versus +66 a month ago, and Hang Seng is at a maximum short of -100.

Vol-control funds would add roughly $62.9B over the next month if daily moves average near zero, but would sell $23.2B on a single 5% down day. One-month realized vol of 23.2 is in the 99.8th percentile versus 15.4 for 3-month realized, and the -4.4% day of Nov 5 is set to drop out of the window.

Goldman Prime data shows fundamental L/S net leverage fell 7.6 points MTD to 41.6%, a 5-year low, and gross leverage fell 4.4 points to 206.3%. Trailing 4-week de-grossing in global equities is the largest since Feb 2023, and long sales outpaced short sales roughly 3 to 1 in November.

Selling of global Info Tech over six weeks is 'by far the fastest in the past 10 years' at -4.4 standard deviations. The sector's long/short ratio is 1.79 versus a YTD peak of 2.9. Net exposure to Semis & Semi Equip fell below Software for the first time since the start of 2026.

Medium-term Momentum exposure is on track for a 6th straight monthly decline to the lowest since Dec 2022, and Value exposure is at 5-year highs 'amid increased stagflation concerns'. Global fundamental L/S funds are down 0.2% in November (+8.9% YTD) and TMT funds are down 4.5% MTD (+0.6% YTD).

Goldman says the market 'could be setting up for a tactical rally in the near term', but its Sentiment Indicator and Risk Appetite Indicator do not show capitulation by a broader set of participants. Professionals have de-risked and the broader investor base has not.

McElligott says the pain-trade rally thesis is 'increasingly HYPER socialized' because it 'makes too much sense'. Index call skews have started to firm and Nomura's desk saw VIX downside put-spread trades over recent sessions. Early Thursday showed a re-gross into legacy themes (DRAM +5.0%, semis +3.4%), which reversed later, including AMD down 11% on a Hunterbrook report.

McElligott prefers dispersion as the way to play a reversal. XLK 3-month implied correlation is at 46.4, a 99th percentile reading and 2.2 standard deviations above its 29.4 mean, and dispersion had a 'TOUGH' week as index vol squeezed against single names.

The macro tape signals a growth scare. The Bloomberg Commodity Index is down 8.5% MTD, energy is down 13.4%, industrial metals are down 8%, Treasuries are rallying and defensives are bid. Financial conditions are 'tightening rapidly' on higher real rates, wider credit spreads and a realized vol shock. McElligott concedes part of this may be mechanical de-grossing rather than a true growth signal.

McElligott says the market now views Nvidia as a 'de facto SHORT Put for the market' where it was previously a 'LONG Put for the ecosystem'. He also flags wealth-effect risk: stocks are the largest component of household wealth, and dip-buyers could rebalance into bonds.

McElligott's test is that if equities still cannot stabilize early next week despite the mechanical buying flows, it signals that 'somebody wants OUT', that the growth scare is real and that 401k and real-money allocators are shifting into fixed income. The article leans toward this darker scenario and notes EPFR data showing retail still buying global equities at a 99.9th percentile pace last week.

risk_factors: The relief-rally view is so widely held that it could fail and leave 'Sellers are LOWER' if spot keeps breaking.
A single 5% down day would trigger about $23.2B of vol-control selling and reset the clock on re-leveraging.
Broader investors, including retail and 401k money, have not capitulated per Goldman's Sentiment and Risk Appetite Indicators, so they remain a source of selling.
Growth scare and tightening financial conditions from higher real rates, wider credit spreads and a realized vol shock.
Wealth-effect risk: stocks are the largest component of household wealth, and dip-buyers could rebalance into bonds.
Leveraged funds remain 'VaR-tied' into the year-end window.
Further single-name shocks such as AMD's 11% drop on a Hunterbrook report.
vol_and_positioning: Dealers remain in a 'significant Short Gamma' market into next week. Some of the gamma rolling off at Friday's expiry is dealer long gamma, so stabilizing flow is lost.
Vol of vol is high, with 60-day realized vol of VVIX at a 2-year high. Skew is steep and call skews have started to firm.
One-month realized vol is 23.2, in the 99.8th percentile, versus 15.4 for 3-month realized. Roll-off of the -4.4% day on Nov 5 should lower realized vol.

CTA model: $7.9B of global equity futures buying on a 2% rally, $21.1B on a 4% rally ($9.3B in the S&P). Trend signals are at -8 for the S&P, Russell, Nasdaq, Nikkei, TOPIX and FTSE, and -100 for the Hang Seng.
Vol-control funds would add about $62.9B over the next month if daily moves average near zero and sell $23.2B on a 5% down day.
Goldman Prime: fundamental L/S net leverage is 41.6% (5-year low) and gross leverage is 206.3%. Global equity de-grossing over 4 weeks is the largest since Feb 2023.
XLK 3-month implied correlation is 46.4 (99th percentile, 29.4 mean), which supports dispersion trades.

VIX downside trades seen by Nomura's desk: 11k and 14k Dec 19/16 put spreads at $0.87 and $0.79, a 4k x 8k Dec 19/17 1x2 put spread at $0.46, a 40k Jan 20/19 put spread at $0.54, and a Dec 22/19 put spread at $1.73.

UBS's note 'The Stock Market Is The Economy Now' is cited for stocks being the largest component of household wealth.

tension_points.bull_case: Dealers, CTAs and vol-control funds are mechanically positioned to buy on a vol reset or rally ($21.1B CTA buying on a 4% move, $62.9B vol-control add), and Goldman Prime shows hedge fund net leverage at a 5-year low, with Goldman flagging a possible tactical rally.
tension_points.bear_case: The rally thesis is 'hyper socialized', Goldman's Sentiment and Risk Appetite Indicators show broader investors have not capitulated, and the S&P failed to hold its 200-day average despite a clean event-risk clearing. A failure to rally would signal that 'somebody wants OUT' and that the growth scare is real.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If by early next week the equity tape still cannot stabilize and move higher despite the mechanical buying flows, McElligott reads that as a real growth scare with larger forces at play.
